President Donald Trump has criticized NBA star LeBron James for not standing still during the national anthem before a Philadelphia 76ers game. The incident occurred during the team's season opener in New York, where James appeared to continue his warm-up exercises while the Star-Spangled Banner was played. Trump shared a video of the moment on social media, calling James a 'TOTAL DISGRACE' and demanding he apologize to American military personnel and those who died for the flag. This is not the first time Trump and James have exchanged public criticism; their feud dates back to 2017 when James wore mismatched shoes with 'equality' written on them and criticized Trump's leadership. James has consistently spoken out on social issues, including during the Black Lives Matter movement, and has been recognized for encouraging voter participation. He has also rejected criticism from figures like Zlatan Ibrahimovic, who suggested athletes should 'just do what you do best' rather than engage in political activism. The 41-year-old James, in his 24th NBA season, was set to play his home debut for the Sixers against Cleveland on the same day Trump made his comments. The controversy highlights the ongoing tension between athletes and political figures regarding the role of sports in social and political discourse.
